glossary.Glomerulus: The tiny knot of capillaries in each nephron that filters blood to make urine.
glossary.Glycaemic control: How well blood glucose is kept in the target range, usually judged by HbA1c.
glossary.Albuminuria: Albumin (a blood protein) leaking into the urine, a sign of a damaged kidney filter.
glossary.Serum albumin: The main protein in blood plasma; low levels cause oedema.
glossary.Early morning specimen: The first urine passed after waking, most concentrated and best for ACR.
glossary.Nephrology: The medical specialty that manages kidney disease.
glossary.Intraglomerular pressure: The blood pressure inside the glomerular capillaries that drives filtration.
glossary.Intraglomerular hypertension: Abnormally high pressure inside the glomerulus, which damages the filter over time.
glossary.Thiazide-like diuretic: A diuretic acting on the distal tubule that lowers blood pressure, such as indapamide.
glossary.Diuretic: A drug that increases urine output by making the kidney excrete more salt and water.
glossary.Statin: A cholesterol-lowering drug used to cut cardiovascular risk.
glossary.Renal transplant: Surgery to place a donor kidney in a patient with kidney failure.
glossary.Histology: Study of tissue under a microscope, for example on a kidney biopsy.
glossary.Basement membrane: A thin layer of matrix under cells; in the glomerulus it is part of the filter.
glossary.Mesangium: Supporting cells and matrix between glomerular capillaries.
glossary.Angiotensin II: A hormone in the RAAS that constricts arterioles, especially the efferent one.
glossary.Aldosterone: Adrenal hormone that makes the kidney retain sodium and water.
glossary.Vasoconstriction: Narrowing of a blood vessel, reducing blood flow through it.
glossary.Arteriole: A small artery; the afferent brings blood into the glomerulus and the efferent takes it out.
glossary.Overt proteinuria: Protein loss large enough to show on standard dipstick tests, a later stage than microalbuminuria.
glossary.Type 1 diabetes: Autoimmune destruction of pancreatic beta cells causing absolute insulin deficiency.
glossary.Type 2 diabetes: Diabetes from insulin resistance with relative insulin deficiency, linked to obesity.
glossary.Cardiovascular disease: Disease of the heart and blood vessels, such as heart attack and stroke.
glossary.Renoprotection: Treatment that slows kidney damage, such as ACE inhibitors or SGLT2 inhibitors.
glossary.Permeability: How easily substances pass through a barrier, such as the glomerular filter.
glossary.Gold standard: The best available test or treatment against which others are judged.
glossary.mg/mmol: Units for ACR: milligrams of albumin per millimole of creatinine.
glossary.Creatinine: A muscle breakdown product cleared by the kidneys; used to estimate kidney function.
glossary.Hypertension: Persistently raised blood pressure, both a cause and result of kidney damage.
